title: 梦江南（梳洗罢）
titleEn: Dreaming of the South: Done with Her Morning Toilet
author: 温庭筠
intro: A woman waits all day in a riverside tower for the boat that will bring her man home. Hundreds of sails go by; none is his. Just 27 characters, and one of the most loved short lyrics in Chinese.
analysis: 这首小词只有二十七个字，写一个女子等待远方的爱人。早上她梳洗打扮好，一个人靠在江边的楼上张望。“独”字说明她是孤单的。江上一只只船开过去，“过尽千帆皆不是”——上千条船都过去了，却没有一条是他的。这一句写出了从希望到失望、一次又一次的心情，是全词最有名的一句。从早上等到傍晚，斜阳的光好像含情脉脉地看着她，江水却悠悠地流走，不管她的心事。最后一句“肠断白蘋洲”，她望着长满白蘋的小洲，伤心得好像肠子都断了（“肠断”是古人形容极度悲伤的说法）。整首词没有写她的长相，只写她的动作和看到的景物，等待的苦却非常真切。
analysisEn: In only 27 characters, this lyric tells of a woman waiting for her absent lover. In the morning she finishes washing and doing her hair, then leans alone on the railing of a tower above the river. The word 独 (“alone”) sets the tone. Boats pass one after another — “a thousand sails go by, and none of them is his.” That line holds a whole day of hope rising and falling, sail after sail, and it is the most quoted line in the piece. By evening the slanting sunlight seems to linger on her tenderly, while the river just flows on, indifferent to her. The last line takes her eyes to a sandbar covered in white duckweed, perhaps where they once parted, and she is “broken-hearted” — literally, her insides torn, the classical way of saying unbearable grief. Notice that we never learn what she looks like or what she thinks; we only see what she does and what she sees, and that is enough to feel her waiting. The landscape does the speaking for her, a technique called “expressing feeling through scenery”.
background: Wen Tingyun (c. 812–866) was one of the first major writers of ci, lyrics written to fixed tunes, and is regarded as a founder of the ornate Huajian (“Among the Flowers”) school. Like many lyrics of his time, this one is written in the voice of a woman.
pronunciation: 脉脉 mò mò（不读 mài mài）；斜 xié；蘋 pín（白蘋：一种水草，不是“苹果”的苹）。机器朗读易错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行教材版本，单调二十七字。词牌《梦江南》又名《忆江南》《望江南》。“白蘋洲”有版本作“白苹洲”，此处的“蘋”是水草名，保留繁体写法以免与“苹果”混淆，与通行教材一致。

lines.py: shū xǐ bà, dú yǐ wàng jiāng lóu
lines.lit: Washing and combing done, alone she leans in the river-viewing tower.
lines.en: Hair combed, face washed, she leans alone in the tower above the river.

lines.py: guò jìn qiān fān jiē bù shì
lines.lit: A thousand sails pass by — all are not it;
lines.en: A thousand sails go by, and none is his.

lines.py: xié huī mò mò shuǐ yōu yōu
lines.lit: the slanting sunlight lingers tenderly, the water flows on and on.
lines.en: The low sun lingers, tender; the river runs on, unhurried.

lines.lit: Heart broken at the islet of white duckweed.
lines.en: Her heart breaks at the sandbar white with duckweed.

words.en: to comb one’s hair and wash one’s face
words.note: 现代汉语仍用，如“梳洗打扮”。
古义“完了”，今天还说“吃罢饭”（书面），口语说“完”。
现代汉语说“靠”，如“倚着栏杆”也还用。

words.en: a thousand sails — i.e. very many boats

words.note: 现代汉语说“都”，成语“人人皆知”里还用。

words.en: slanting rays of the setting sun

words.note: 今天常说“含情脉脉”。注意读 mò。

words.en: slow and long; on and on
words.note: 现代汉语仍用，如“白云悠悠”。
古人形容极度悲伤；今天常说“断肠”“肝肠寸断”。

words.en: white duckweed, a small floating water plant
words.note: 一种浮在水面开白花的水草。

imagery.name: 楼
imagery.zh: 江边的高楼是她天天登上去张望的地方，登得越高，望得越远，盼得越苦。
imagery.en: The riverside tower is where she climbs each day to watch; the higher she stands, the further she looks, the harder she waits.

imagery.name: 帆
imagery.zh: 一只只船帆带来希望又带走希望，“千帆”写出失望了无数次。
imagery.en: Each sail raises her hope and then takes it away — a thousand sails mean a thousand small disappointments.

imagery.name: 夕阳
imagery.zh: 斜阳说明她从早等到了晚；阳光“脉脉”，好像懂她的心事。
imagery.en: The slanting sun shows she has waited from morning to evening; its light seems to understand her.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 江水悠悠流走，不停留、不回应，像离开的人一样远去。
imagery.en: The river keeps flowing away without pausing or answering — like the man who left.
